sn56.48:1.1: “Bhikkhus, suppose that this great earth had become one mass of water,
sn56.48:1.2: and a man would throw a yoke with a single hole upon it.
sn56.48:1.3: An easterly wind would drive it westward; a westerly wind would drive it eastward; a northerly wind would drive it southward; a southerly wind would drive it northward.
sn56.48:1.4: There was a blind turtle which would come to the surface once every hundred years.
sn56.48:1.6: would that blind turtle, coming to the surface once every hundred years, insert its neck into that yoke with a single hole?” “It would be by chance, venerable sir, that that blind turtle, coming to the surface once every hundred years, would insert its neck into that yoke with a single hole.”
sn56.48:2.1: “So too, bhikkhus, it is by chance that one obtains the human state;
sn56.48:2.2: by chance that a Tathagata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One arises in the world;
sn56.48:2.3: by chance that the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathagata shines in the world.
sn56.48:2.4: “You have obtained that human state, bhikkhus; a Tathagata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One has arisen in the world; the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathagata shines in the world.
sn56.48:3.1: “Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering.’… An exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’”
